a) we introduce a novel mechanism to provide haptic sensation for touch-based applications that use body-carried electric charges to provide physical stimuli, and b) we explore the design space for interactions using our proposed mechanism, and demonstrate two applications to show its feasibility.
we propose a wearable haptics device that uses body-channels to provide physical stimuli, and we explore the design space for body-channel haptics using two novel applications.

we propose a haptic feedback device using electrostatic force that does not require physical actuation of objects, nor hand-worn haptics, and can be used to provide haptic sensations for mobile applications leveraging intra- or body-channels.

exploring the potential of electrostatic force as a novel haptic feedback modality for body area networks.
